newsitem.title: GERMANY: German aluminium outlook bright after steady sales.
newsitem.headline: German aluminium outlook bright after steady sales.

text.p: Germany's aluminium sector expected steady sales in 1996 after just under 21 billion marks in 1995 following improved business in the second half, the GDA industry association said on Tuesday.
"New orders have been stabilising since the middle of the year after a weak first half and are now increasing," GDA president Walter Hueck told a news conference.

Hueck said in April he had expected lower sales values for the full year because of a downturn in the building industry, which depressed sales of aluminium semis and fabricated products for construction.
But the general economic climate was now more encouraging and aluminium demand from the transport sector was holding up well, he said at the news conference.
At the meeting GDA also supplied details of first half production figures in various product categories.
Aluminium semis output in Jan-June was down by 3.4 percent from the same 1995 period at 773,230 tonnes, the association said.
Aluminium castings production in Jan-June 1996 was 1.6 percent lower at 246,840 tonnes.
Foil and narrow strip manufacturers said first half 1996 production was off 10.3 percent at 93,960 tonnes.
Primary aluminium production in the six months under review was up 2.5 percent at 287,700 tonnes and secondary production down 6.8 percent at 216,500 tonnes.
